title: Log-concavity and positive dependence in Sine-β and Hua–Pickrell processes
shortTitle: Cut the circle at the origin: the Johnston–Prochno conjecture for every β
oneLine: Eigenvalue patterns of large random matrices (the Sine-β process): for every β, points counted from a fixed origin have log-concave, positively dependent joint laws, proving a 2024 conjecture; the typical spacing obeys Gamma bounds of optimal shape β+1, so its variance is at most 1/(β+1).
abstract: Eigenvalues of a large random matrix, seen on the scale of one spacing, form the same random pattern for a very wide range of models: the Sine-β point process, where β measures how strongly neighbouring points repel. Johnston and Prochno (2024) conjectured that, for the sine process (β = 2), points numbered outward from a fixed origin have log-concave joint densities. Edge results did not reach the middle of the spectrum, because there the number of points to the left of the origin is random and mixtures of log-concave laws need not be log-concave. This candidate cuts the circular β-ensemble at the origin, so that every origin label becomes a fixed coordinate, and passes to the limit. For every β > 0 it proves that every finite vector of origin-labelled points has a log-concave density and is multivariate totally positive (MTP₂), and that this survives division by the β-th power of the Vandermonde product of the selected points, also for the process seen from a typical point. Consequently the mean-one typical spacing G is dominated in convex order by Gamma(β+1, β+1), so Var(G) ≤ 1/(β+1); the shape β+1 is optimal, small gaps have probability of exact order t^(β+1), and the variance bound becomes exact as β → 0. The same comparison holds for any normalised eigenvalue difference in a finite β-ensemble with convex potential, at every size. For the Hua–Pickrell process with charge δ, labelled laws are MTP₂ for Re δ > −1/2 and log-concave exactly when Re δ ≥ 0; at the hard edge, the positive labelled points are log-concave for a ≥ 1/β − 1. At β = 2 the variance bound is 1/3 against the true 0.180, and large-gap bounds are far from the truth. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Theorem 2.1 (proof): for every β > 0, every finite vector of origin-labelled Sine-β points has a log-concave density, positive on its ordered sign chamber, and is MTP₂. At β = 2 this proves Johnston–Prochno, arXiv:2410.10754v2, Conjecture 2.2.
Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.3 (proof): the density divided by Δ^β, and for Palm labels by Δ^β ∏|x_r|^β, is log-concave and MTP₂; the typical-spacing density p satisfies: p(s)/s^β is log-concave.

Theorem 2.4 and Proposition 2.5 (proof): G ⪯cx Gamma(β+1, β+1), so Var(G) ≤ 1/(β+1), E 1/G ≤ (β+1)/β and both tails are at most (t e^(1−t))^(β+1); the shape β+1 is optimal, P(G ≤ t) is of exact order t^(β+1), and (β+1)Var(G) → 1 as β → 0.

Theorem 2.6 and Corollary 2.7 (proof): for finite β-ensembles with convex potential, every normalised eigenvalue difference is dominated by Gamma(β+1, β+1) at every size; for GUE gaps this improves the moment bounds of Johnston (2026) for every p > 1 and the tail bounds for h > 2.15 and h < 0.31.

Theorem 2.8 (proof): Hua–Pickrell labelled laws are MTP₂ for Re δ > −1/2 and log-concave exactly when Re δ ≥ 0 (as laws; densities at β = 2); Proposition 2.9: the positive hard-edge labelled points are log-concave for a ≥ 1/β − 1 and MTP₂ for every a.

narration: Cut the circle at the origin. An Evidence Press briefing. Look at the eigenvalues of a large random matrix, on the scale of one gap between neighbours, and the same random pattern appears for a very wide range of models. It is called the sine-beta process. The number beta measures how strongly neighbouring points repel. Exact formulas for this pattern are rare, so shape properties that hold for every beta are valuable. In twenty twenty-four, Johnston and Prochno conjectured that if you number the points outward from a fixed origin, any selection of them has a log-concave joint law: a single-peaked, well-concentrated shape. Near the edge of the spectrum this was known, because the k-th point from the edge is a fixed coordinate. In the middle it was not, because how many points lie to the left of the origin is random, and mixing log-concave laws can spoil log-concavity. The idea of this release is to put the particles on a circle and cut the circle at the origin. Then the first point to the right of the origin is simply the first coordinate, with nothing random about the labelling. On the cut circle, log-concavity and a strong form of positive dependence hold, and both survive the limit. So the conjecture is proved, for every beta. A stronger version keeps the repulsion between points. As a consequence, the typical spacing is less spread out than a Gamma variable of shape beta plus one, so its variance is at most one over beta plus one. That shape cannot be improved. The same bounds hold at every size for finite matrix ensembles with a convex potential. There is also an exact threshold when a charge sits at the origin, and a new range at the hard edge. Now the limits. At beta equal to two, the variance bound is one third, against a true value of about nought point one eight. For very large gaps the bounds are weak: the bound on a gap three times the mean is about seven in a hundred, while the truth is about five in a hundred thousand. Nothing here concerns zeros of the Riemann zeta function, and the exact hard-edge threshold remains open. The proofs rely on strong known limit theorems. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, published on the fourteenth of November twenty twenty-six. Its review was internal and AI-assisted, not peer review. The paper, the checking scripts and the evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

decisionObject.description: Treat origin-labelled Sine-β marginals as log-concave and MTP₂ for every β, and the typical spacing as dominated in convex order by Gamma(β+1, β+1) with optimal shape; treat Re δ ≥ 0 as the exact log-concavity threshold for Hua–Pickrell limits.
decisionObject.scope: Sine-β at intensity one and its Palm version; finite β-ensembles with convex potential; Hua–Pickrell limits as laws (densities at β = 2); hard-edge points for a ≥ 1/β − 1. Gap-vector dependence, sums of spacings, large-gap asymptotics and hard-edge necessity are not settled.
